checkedAlternates.risk: Mayonnaise and Hollandaise both use egg yolks as emulsifiers.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Mayonnaise is a cold emulsion using neutral vegetable oil (group-1), whereas Hollandaise and Béarnaise are warm clarified-butter emulsions (group-2).

checkedAlternates.risk: Velouté and Béchamel are both thickened with a roux.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Velouté uses light poultry/fish/veal stock (group-3), whereas Béchamel uses milk (group-4).
